summary: Instagram is carrying almost all the attention: the Hindi videos get 100 to 1,400 views there, while YouTube gives most of them under 25 views. The best video by far is the PIR motion sensor one, which hooks people with a surprising 'it doesn't actually see you' claim about a device they meet daily. Weaker videos cover abstract or less visible topics (smartwatch, ultrasonic, TV remote) and get views but almost no likes, shares or saves. The only English video did a bit better on YouTube than most Hindi ones, but the sample is just one video.
winningPattern: Everyday device people see in daily life (motion sensor, street light) + a myth-busting or 'it doesn't work how you think' hook in Hinglish + a question title ending with 🤔 #shorts, posted mainly for Instagram Reels. The PIR video also worked on YouTube, so a strong surprising opening line matters more than anything else.
doMore: Open with a surprising negative claim ('X doesn't actually see/hear/feel...') then explain how it really works
Pick devices viewers touch or walk past every day: lifts, ATMs, fans, AC remotes, car parking sensors
Put the key hook line big on screen in the first second and keep the title as one clear question
Lead with Instagram Reels and cross-post to YouTube, checking which sensor topics also get YouTube views
End each video with a share or save prompt like 'Dost ko bhejo jo yeh nahi jaanta' since shares and saves are the strongest signal
Test a few English-narrated versions of the best Hindi topics to compare against the single English data point
stopDoing: Stop picking abstract or invisible-feeling topics with no familiar object in the scene (smartwatch light, ultrasonic bat comparison)
Stop publishing near-duplicate topics close together (two smoke alarm videos in days split the audience)
Stop judging by views alone; videos with views but zero shares and saves are not building a following
